chapter: Boyhood in Evergreen and Calhoun school
title: Switching to lead trumpet when the men went to war
summary: When Theophilus left for the Army he moved to trumpet and led the town band at about 14, the youngest member, to his mother's worry.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Well, he played the baritone and trumpet. In fact he was playing trumpet up until it got time to go into the Army in the First World War, and I was playing the peck horn, and I had to switch to the trumpet, and I
was able to and strong enough to play lead trumpet because they had no trumpet player in the band.
That was your first experience with the trumpet then?
Yeah. And afterwards I switched over and started playing -- I knew all the marches anyway, and --
You must have been what, about 14 at that time?

Yes, close to it, because when they went up to go to the Army, to go to war, I was playing in the -- of course, my mother didn't like that because all the men in the band, the old men with the handlebar mustache --
And everytime she says, they're out there killing my poor child, blowing his brains out and what --
-- because every time they'd have a kind of a convention, Sunday school convention or whatnot, whatever, they'd have the band come out, you know, and play and --
Were you the youngest one in the band then?
Von and there was -- were there 20 year olds too in it?
Oh, well, they were much older. They
were like my father, you know, much older.
How was it? It went all the way up to much older people, but I suppose there were some in between.

Well, the leader's son, he and I was about the same -- were about the same age, and he played trumpet, but they had to take him out. He was too weak. He was physically weak, you know. I think the doctors told him no, but I kept on.
